title: Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance: Advanced Research Opportunities in Economics, Finance, Business and Law
summary: Introduction The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an opportunity for students seeking advanced specialisation and research training in economics, finance, law and business. The programme is designed for individuals who wish to pursue academic or professional careers in institutions where advanced economic, financial, business or statistical knowledge is required. Through its research-focused approach, the programme aims to advance knowledge in economics, business and the social sciences while contributing to the analysis of important economic problems. It provides students with the tools needed to conduct advanced research, examine complex economic issues and formulate economic alternatives and policies that can contribute to economic development. The programme brings together four main research areas: Economics, Finance, Business and Law. These areas provide a broad foundation for investigating economic and financial challenges, developing new knowledge and exploring solutions to issues affecting businesses, institutions and society. In addition to its academic and research objectives, the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an international learning environment, experienced faculty, opportunities for research collaboration and an intellectually stimulating atmosphere that encourages critical thinking and cooperation. About the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is intended for students who want to develop advanced expertise in areas related to economics, finance, law and business. Its objective is to prepare individuals for careers that require a strong understanding of economic and financial systems, analytical methods, statistical techniques and research. The programme is particularly relevant to people interested in working in academic institutions, central banks, research departments, public-sector organisations, private-sector entities and other institutions that rely on advanced economic, financial or statistical skills. A central objective of the programme is to contribute to the advancement of knowledge. Through doctoral-level research, students can investigate important economic and social questions, develop new insights and contribute to discussions about economic development and policy. The programme also seeks to equip researchers with the tools required to conduct research at the frontier of knowledge. This emphasis on advanced research enables students to explore existing economic challenges, examine alternative approaches and contribute evidence that may inform economic decisions and policies. Objectives of the Doctoral Programme The programme has several interconnected objectives that guide its academic and research activities. 1. Provide Advanced Specialisation The programme offers advanced specialisation in Economics, Finance, Law and Business. This allows students to develop deeper knowledge in their chosen research area and acquire expertise relevant to academic research or professional work. Advanced specialisation is particularly important in institutions where economic decisions, financial analysis, statistical research and policy development require a high level of technical knowledge. 2. Prepare Students for Academic and Professional Careers The programme is designed for individuals who intend to pursue academic or professional careers. For those interested in academia, doctoral research provides an opportunity to develop research skills and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in their chosen field. For those pursuing professional careers, the programme aims to develop advanced analytical and research capabilities that can be applied in institutions such as central banks, public and private research departments, and other organisations. 3. Advance Economic, Business and Social Knowledge Another important objective is to advance the frontier of knowledge in economics, business and the social sciences. The programme encourages research that contributes to a deeper understanding of economic and social issues. By investigating relevant problems and developing new findings, doctoral researchers can help expand the knowledge available to academics, policymakers, businesses and other institutions. 4. Analyse Important Economic Problems The programme seeks to contribute to the analysis of the most relevant economic problems. Economic challenges often involve complex relationships between markets, institutions, financial systems, businesses and society. Doctoral research can help investigate these relationships, identify underlying issues and develop a more detailed understanding of the problems being examined. 5. Develop Research-Based Economic Alternatives and Policies The programme provides the tools needed to carry out advanced research that can support the formulation of economic alternatives and policies geared towards economic development. This objective connects academic research with practical economic questions. Through research, students can examine different approaches to economic challenges and contribute knowledge that may help inform policy discussions and development strategies. The Four Research Areas The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is organised around four research lines: Economics, Finance, Business and Law. These areas provide the programme s central fields of academic specialisation. 1. Economics The Economics research line provides a foundation for investigating economic issues and contributing to the understanding of how economies function. Research in economics can be relevant to questions involving economic development, public policy, markets, institutions and broader economic challenges. The programme s stated objective of analysing important economic problems makes this research area particularly relevant to students interested in producing knowledge that can inform economic alternatives and policies. Economics research can also support careers in academic institutions, central banks, research departments and other organisations that require advanced economic expertise. 2. Finance The Finance research line is relevant to students interested in advanced financial analysis and research. Financial knowledge is important in institutions that examine financial systems, evaluate economic and financial conditions, and make decisions that require specialised analytical skills. The programme s emphasis on advanced financial and statistical capabilities makes this research line relevant to individuals seeking careers in financial institutions, central banks, research departments and other organisations. Through doctoral research, students can pursue specialised questions within finance and contribute to the development of knowledge in the field. 3. Business The Business research line provides an opportunity to investigate issues related to businesses and their economic and social environments. Business research can contribute to a better understanding of organisational and economic challenges and support the development of knowledge relevant to professional and academic settings. The programme s broader objective of advancing business and social knowledge means that this research line forms part of its contribution to understanding important issues affecting institutions and the economy. 4. Law The Law research line provides a further area of specialisation within the doctoral programme. Its inclusion reflects the programme s broad approach to advanced study across economics, finance, law and business. It offers a research pathway for students whose academic interests involve legal questions connected to the programme s wider fields of study. Together, the four research lines create a broad academic structure through which doctoral students can pursue specialised research and contribute to knowledge in their chosen area. Faculty with International Research Experience and Recognition One of the programme s stated features is its faculty, which has international research experience and recognition. An experienced research faculty can contribute to an academic environment in which students engage with advanced ideas, develop research questions and strengthen their understanding of their chosen fields. The programme s emphasis on international research experience also reflects its commitment to connecting doctoral study with wider academic research. This is relevant to students who want to undertake advanced research and develop expertise that can be applied in academic or professional institutions. The programme identifies its faculty as an important part of the learning and research environment it offers. An International Academic Environment The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an international environment that enables it to attract students from different countries. An international academic environment can bring together individuals with different educational experiences, perspectives and research interests. This can create opportunities for academic exchange and discussion across different economic, financial, business and legal contexts. The programme s international orientation is also reflected in its emphasis on research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions. For students interested in developing an international academic or professional outlook, this environment forms an important part of the programme s overall offering. However, the programme information provided does not specify particular eligible countries, nationality requirements or geographical restrictions. Prospective applicants should contact the programme directly if they require confirmation of country-specific eligibility. Research Opportunities at the Frontier of Knowledge The programme offers what it describes as an attractive set of research lines linked to the frontier of knowledge in different areas. Research at the frontier of knowledge involves engaging with current questions and developing work that can contribute to the advancement of a field. Within this programme, the four research lines provide the broad areas in which students can pursue specialised academic research. The programme s research orientation is closely connected to its objective of advancing economic, business and social knowledge. Rather than focusing only on the acquisition of existing knowledge, it aims to provide the tools needed for students to conduct research and contribute new insights. This focus is particularly relevant for individuals who want to develop advanced research capabilities for academic careers or professional roles that involve complex analysis. An Intellectually Active and Stimulating Research Environment The programme places emphasis on creating an intellectually active and stimulating atmosphere. Its academic environment is designed to encourage critical thinking, cooperation and joint research. These elements are important in doctoral study, where students are expected to engage deeply with research questions, assess ideas critically and contribute to the development of knowledge. The programme also fosters international research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions, alongside cooperative research programmes. These activities reflect an approach to doctoral education that values collaboration and engagement with the wider research community. Critical Thinking Critical thinking is an important part of advanced research. Researchers must be able to examine questions carefully, assess evidence, consider different explanations and develop reasoned conclusions. The programme s emphasis on critical thinking supports its objective of preparing students to analyse relevant economic problems and contribute to the advancement of knowledge. Cooperation and Joint Research The programme also emphasises cooperation and joint research. Research collaboration allows scholars to exchange ideas, work together on questions of shared interest and draw on different areas of expertise. The programme s focus on cooperation is consistent with its wider aim of creating an active academic environment. International Research Exchanges International research exchanges provide opportunities for engagement with leading universities and research institutions. The programme identifies these exchanges, together with cooperative research programmes, as part of the academic environment it seeks to foster. These connections can support the exchange of research ideas and contribute to a broader understanding of developments in economics, finance, business and law. APPLY HERE Who Should Consider the Doctoral Programme? The programme is intended for students who wish to pursue advanced specialisation and research in Economics, Finance, Law or Business. It may be particularly relevant to individuals who are interested in: Pursuing an academic career involving teaching or research. Developing advanced expertise in economics, finance, business or law. Working in central banks or economic and financial institutions. Joining research departments in public or private organisations. Conducting research on important economic and social problems. Contributing to the development of economic alternatives and policies. Building advanced analytical, financial, economic or statistical skills. The programme s stated purpose is to prepare students for academic and professional careers that require advanced skills. The information provided does not specify the precise academic qualifications, grades, language requirements, professional experience or other admission criteria. Applicants should request the official admission requirements directly from the programme. Career Relevance and Potential Professional Pathways The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is designed to develop expertise relevant to institutions that require advanced economic, financial or statistical skills. The programme specifically identifies several types of institutions in which such expertise may be useful. Academic Institutions Students interested in academic careers can use doctoral research to develop specialised knowledge and research capabilities. The programme s emphasis on advancing knowledge, critical thinking and joint research is relevant to individuals who intend to contribute to academic research. Central Banks Central banks are among the institutions identified in the programme description as requiring advanced skills in economic, financial or statistical fields. The programme s research areas and focus on economic problem analysis are relevant to individuals interested in developing expertise for work in such institutions. Public and Private Research Departments The programme also identifies research departments in public and private entities as potential professional settings. These organisations may require people who can conduct advanced research, analyse complex issues and contribute to evidence-based work. The programme s emphasis on research methods and the development of economic knowledge is aligned with these broad professional needs. Other Organisations Requiring Advanced Expertise The programme is also intended for students who wish to work in other organisations that require advanced economic, financial or statistical skills. The range of research lines means that the programme is not limited to one professional sector. Its relevance will depend on the student s research specialisation and the requirements of the institution or career they intend to pursue. These are potential career pathways identified by the programme s stated objectives, not guarantees of employment after graduation. How to Obtain Further Information Individuals who would like to learn more about the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance can contact the programme directly by email. Email: doctoralprogrammes@cunef.edu Prospective applicants can use this contact to request further information about the programme, including its admission requirements, application process, research opportunities and other details not included in the general programme description. Before making an application, interested students should seek confirmation of the academic qualifications required, the application timeline, any applicable fees or funding arrangements, and the documents that must be submitted. Visit HERE to learn more about the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance Application Deadline and Funding Information The programme information provided does not state an application deadline. It also does not specify whether the doctoral programme offers scholarships, tuition waivers, stipends or other financial support. Prospective applicants should contact the programme directly to confirm the current application period, fees and any available funding opportunities. Conclusion The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers advanced specialisation and research opportunities across Economics, Finance, Business and Law. It is designed for students who wish to pursue academic or professional careers in institutions that require advanced economic, financial or statistical expertise. Its central objectives include advancing economic, business and social knowledge, analysing important economic problems, and providing the tools needed to conduct research that can contribute to economic alternatives and development-oriented policies. The programme s international research faculty, international academic environment, research lines and emphasis on critical thinking, cooperation and joint research form the foundation of its academic offering. It also seeks to foster research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions and to encourage cooperative research programmes. For individuals interested in doctoral-level research and careers in academia, central banking, public or private research departments, and other institutions requiring advanced expertise, the programme may be worth exploring. Those interested in pursuing this opportunity should contact doctoralprogrammes@cunef.edu for further details about admission requirements, application procedures, deadlines, fees and potential funding opportunities. title: 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship: A 12-Month Opportunity to Gain U.S. Congressional Policy and Legislative Experience
summary: The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship offers an opportunity for individuals interested in public policy, government, legislation, and civic engagement to gain practical experience within the United States Congress. The fellowship places participants in a congressional office or committee for 12 months, where they undertake work comparable to that of a congressional legislative aide. The programme is designed to help fellows develop a deeper understanding of the legislative process, gain practical policy experience, build professional networks, and develop skills that can be applied to future careers in congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, and the private sector. The fellowship will run from August 30, 2027, to August 25, 2028 , and will take place in Washington, D.C. The application deadline is December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET . About the APAICS Congressional Fellowship The APAICS Congressional Fellowship is structured around practical participation in the legislative process. Rather than being limited to classroom-based learning, fellows are placed directly within a congressional environment where they can gain experience working on matters related to public policy and legislative activities. During the 12-month fellowship, participants will be placed with either a congressional office or a congressional committee . Their responsibilities will depend on the office or committee where they are placed and the specific policy portfolio assigned to them. The programme states that fellows will undertake work equivalent to that of a congressional legislative aide. This provides fellows with an opportunity to develop practical knowledge of how Congress operates while contributing to the activities of their host office. By completing the fellowship, participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of the U.S. legislative process and establish professional relationships on Capitol Hill. What Fellows Can Gain from the Programme The fellowship is designed to provide participants with professional and policy-related development throughout the programme. One major benefit is the opportunity to gain first-hand experience of the U.S. legislative process . Working within a congressional office or committee allows fellows to observe and participate in the processes through which public policy is discussed and developed. Fellows can also develop professional skills that may be useful beyond the fellowship. According to the programme description, the experience can help fellows acquire skills and expertise that are marketable to congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, and private-sector employers. The programme also provides an opportunity to develop a professional network on Capitol Hill . Because fellows work within congressional environments and participate in APAICS activities, they can interact with professionals involved in public policy and government. Another important aspect is professional development. Fellows are required to meet as a cohort twice every month to discuss their experiences and participate in professional development opportunities. This provides a structured environment in which participants can reflect on their work, exchange experiences, and learn from other fellows. Congressional Office or Committee Placement Each fellow s experience will be different because placements and responsibilities depend on the congressional office or committee to which they are assigned. The policy portfolio given to a fellow will therefore determine much of the day-to-day experience. This means that participants may have different responsibilities depending on the policy issues and legislative work handled by their host office. The programme provides fellows with the opportunity to work in a professional congressional environment while developing an understanding of how Congress functions. This practical component is particularly relevant for individuals who are interested in careers involving public policy, government relations, legislative affairs, advocacy, public administration, international affairs, or related fields. Fellowship Duration and Location The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship will run for approximately 12 months. The programme dates are: Start date: August 30, 2027 End date: August 25, 2028 Location: Washington, D.C. Washington, D.C. is the centre of the U.S. federal government and provides the setting for the fellowship s congressional placement. Participants should therefore be prepared for an extended period in Washington, D.C., rather than a short-term programme. Fellows Are Not Federal Government Employees An important distinction in the programme description is that APAICS Congressional Fellows are not employees of the federal government, their host congressional office, or APAICS . Instead, fellows receive a monthly educational stipend during the fellowship. This distinction is important for applicants to understand because the fellowship provides professional experience within a congressional environment without making the fellow a federal government employee. Cohort Meetings and Professional Development In addition to their work within their assigned congressional offices or committees, fellows are expected to participate in activities organized for the fellowship cohort. Fellows are required to gather twice each month to discuss their experiences and participate in professional development opportunities. These meetings provide an opportunity for participants to learn from one another and discuss the different experiences they encounter during their congressional placements. The fellowship also expects participants to attend events organized by APAICS. These include the organization s Annual Awards Gala and policy summits . Public Policy Presentation Another important requirement of the fellowship is a public presentation. Towards the end of the fellowship year, fellows are required to make a public presentation on a policy topic of their choosing . This requirement gives participants an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding of a policy issue and communicate their ideas publicly after gaining practical experience during the fellowship. The presentation also complements the fellowship s broader emphasis on professional development, policy knowledge, and communication. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The application deadline for the 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship is: December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Applicants should ensure that their application materials are submitted before the stated deadline. The same deadline also applies to the submission of recommendation letters through the recommender portal. The fellowship itself begins on August 30, 2027 , and concludes on August 25, 2028 . How to Apply Applicants are required to submit a complete application containing several components. The application includes: Cover letter expressing interest in the programme. Resume , which must be no more than one page. Academic transcript. Two letters of recommendation. Responses to three application questions. The recommendation letters can be submitted separately by the recommenders through the designated recommendation portal. Applicants should also pay attention to the formatting requirements for the three written responses. Each response should be no more than one page , double-spaced , and written in 12-point Times New Roman font . Application Question One The first question asks applicants to explain how they envision the APAICS Fellowship contributing to their career path and what they hope to gain from the programme. This question gives applicants an opportunity to explain their professional goals and connect those goals to the experience offered by the fellowship. A strong response would therefore need to clearly explain the applicant s career direction, why congressional and public policy experience is relevant to that direction, and what knowledge, skills, or professional experience they hope to develop. Application Question Two The second question focuses specifically on the applicant s experience with Asian American, Native Hawaiian, or Pacific Islander communities in the United States . Applicants are asked to describe when they have lived near or far from these communities and explain how that proximity, or lack of proximity, has shaped their views on public policy. This question requires applicants to reflect on their personal experiences and connect those experiences to their understanding of public policy. Visit HERE to learn more about the 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship Application Question Three The third question focuses on teamwork and problem-solving. Applicants are asked to describe a time when they worked as part of a team and encountered a challenge. They must discuss the challenges they experienced individually and as a team, explain how they contributed to addressing the challenge, and describe what they learned about working with others. This question allows applicants to demonstrate their teamwork, communication, problem-solving, adaptability, and ability to learn from experience. Recommendation Letters Applicants are required to obtain two letters of recommendation . The programme provides a separate online portal where recommenders can submit their letters. The recommendation deadline is the same as the main application deadline: December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET. Applicants should therefore allow sufficient time for their recommenders to complete and submit their letters before the deadline. Why the Fellowship Can Be Relevant to Public Policy Careers The structure of the APAICS Congressional Fellowship provides participants with exposure to several aspects of public policy work. A fellow working within a congressional office or committee can gain an understanding of how legislative institutions operate while developing professional experience in a policy environment. The combination of congressional placement, cohort meetings, professional development, APAICS events, networking opportunities, and a final public policy presentation makes the programme broader than a conventional short-term work placement. The experience can be particularly relevant to people considering future careers involving public policy, legislative affairs, government, nonprofit organizations, federal agencies, advocacy, public administration, or related areas . Important Information for Prospective Applicants Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully review the official fellowship information, eligibility requirements, frequently asked questions, and host office information. Official Application Apply for the 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship Fellowship Details and Eligibility APAICS Fellowship Details and Eligibility Frequently Asked Questions APAICS Fellowship FAQs Host Office FAQs Host Office FAQs Conclusion The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship provides a 12-month opportunity to gain practical experience within the U.S. congressional environment while developing knowledge of public policy and the legislative process. Fellows are placed in congressional offices or committees and undertake work comparable to that of congressional legislative aides, with each placement differing according to the host office and assigned policy portfolio. In addition to their congressional placement, fellows participate in twice-monthly cohort meetings, professional development activities, APAICS events, and a public policy presentation at the end of the fellowship. The programme also provides a monthly educational stipend and opportunities to develop professional networks on Capitol Hill. The fellowship will take place in Washington, D.C., from August 30, 2027, to August 25, 2028 . Interested applicants should prepare the required cover letter, one-page resume, academic transcript, two recommendation letters, and responses to the three application questions before the December 18, 2026, 11:59 PM ET deadline . title: AIBM Graduate Research Fellowship 2026 | $10,000 Per Year for Up to 2 Years
summary: The American Institute for Boys and Men (AIBM) is inviting applications for its Graduate Research Fellowship , supporting emerging scholars conducting rigorous empirical research on issues affecting boys and men. The fellowship provides $10,000 per year for up to two years and is designed to help build a stronger research field and cohort of scholars studying the challenges and opportunities facing boys and men. AIBM describes its work as focused on rigorous, objective and non-partisan research intended to improve the wellbeing of boys and men. For the current fellowship cycle, AIBM is particularly interested in research examining men s employment and labor force participation, online gambling, gaming and pornography, modern fatherhood, and social connection and civic engagement among young men. About the AIBM Graduate Research Fellowship The Graduate Research Fellowship is intended to support graduate researchers whose work aligns with AIBM s mission. The programme welcomes rigorous empirical research on topics related to boys and men , while maintaining particular areas of interest for the current application cycle. AIBM s fellowship programme is part of its broader effort to develop a community of researchers and scholars producing evidence on issues affecting boys and men. Fellowship Award Selected fellows receive: $10,000 per year for up to two years. Based on AIBM s published fellowship information, fellowship funds can support research-related expenses such as: Interviews Fieldwork Experiments Research participants Data purchases Stipend support Conferences Travel Fees Contributions from project collaborators The published fellowship guidelines state that the grants cannot cover indirect overhead . Research Areas of Interest AIBM states that applications can address any topic related to boys and men, provided the proposed work is rigorous and empirical. For the current cycle, the organization has identified several areas of particular interest. 1. Men s Employment and Labor Force Participation AIBM is interested in research examining the causes and consequences of declining employment and labor force participation among men , particularly men without a four-year college degree. Potential research may examine questions related to employment patterns, economic opportunity, workforce participation and the factors affecting men s connection to the labor market. 2. Online Gambling, Gaming and Pornography Another area of interest is understanding the effects of online gambling, gaming and pornography on boys and men . This area aligns with AIBM s broader Boys Men Online initiative, which examines how digital technologies and online environments influence the social, emotional and financial lives of boys and men. The initiative currently studies areas including sports betting, pornography, gaming, AI companions and cryptocurrency/day-trading. 3. Modern Fatherhood AIBM is also seeking research that can contribute to a modern, inclusive, strengths-based vision of fatherhood . This aligns with AIBM s broader Modern Fatherhood initiative, which examines fatherhood, father figures and the role of fathers and other male role models in the lives of boys and young men. 4. Social Connection, Belonging and Civic Engagement The current fellowship call also highlights research that can build evidence for solutions strengthening: Social connection Belonging Civic engagement The particular focus is on young men and approaches that may strengthen their connections to communities and civic life. Who Can Apply? The current AIBM fellowship information indicates that the fellowship is intended for graduate students conducting research aligned with the Institute s mission . AIBM s published fellowship posting specifies that applicants must be currently enrolled in a Ph.D. programme at an accredited university in the United States . The programme welcomes researchers from multiple academic disciplines, including: Economics Political science Sociology Psychology Public policy Education Both qualitative and quantitative research are welcomed. Students may be at the dissertation stage and seeking support, but applicants do not necessarily have to be at the dissertation stage. What Kind of Research Is AIBM Looking For? AIBM s published fellowship information emphasizes research that is: Rigorous Empirical Relevant to boys and men Capable of contributing to the broader field Potentially useful for policy discussions and interventions The Institute s fellowship programme seeks scholars whose research can contribute to understanding challenges and opportunities affecting boys and men and potentially inform policies and practices. Applicants whose proposed topic does not fall neatly within one of the highlighted areas may still apply if they can demonstrate a strong connection to the broader field. Building a Field of Study AIBM s fellowship programme is not only intended to fund individual research projects. The organization also describes the fellowship as part of an effort to build a robust field of study and cohort of scholars focused on boys and men . AIBM currently maintains a community of staff, fellows and student fellows working across areas including education, employment, health, gambling, fatherhood and digital environments. Examples of Research Areas Within AIBM s Broader Work AIBM s existing fellows and student fellows work on a variety of research questions, including: Boys education Men s employment Family and fatherhood Men s health Gambling Online pornography Male teachers Social and emotional development Economic policy Civic outcomes Digital behavior This illustrates the breadth of research that can fall within the organization s wider mission. Application Deadline The current application deadline is: 15 December 2026 The deadline has been confirmed in AIBM s current fellowship announcement and related announcement from AIBM representatives. Applicants should complete and submit their application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. How to Apply Interested graduate researchers should consult the American Institute for Boys and Men Careers and Opportunities page for the current Graduate Research Fellowship application information. Applicants should carefully review the fellowship requirements and ensure that their research proposal clearly explains: The research question. The relevance of the research to boys and men. The empirical approach. The expected contribution to the field. How the research could contribute to policy or practical solutions where appropriate. Tips for Preparing Your Application Clearly Define the Research Question A strong proposal should clearly explain the problem being investigated and why the question matters. Demonstrate Rigorous Research AIBM specifically emphasizes rigorous empirical research, so applicants should clearly explain their proposed methodology and evidence base. Connect the Work to Boys and Men Make the connection between the proposed research and the wellbeing, experiences, opportunities or challenges of boys and men clear. Consider Policy Relevance Research that can contribute to policy discussions or interventions is particularly relevant to the fellowship s stated objectives. Show How the Fellowship Supports the Project Applicants should explain how the fellowship funding would help advance their research, whether through data acquisition, fieldwork, participant recruitment, travel, conferences or other eligible research expenses. Conclusion The AIBM Graduate Research Fellowship offers Ph.D. students an opportunity to receive $10,000 per year for up to two years while conducting research related to boys and men. The current call welcomes rigorous empirical research across a broad range of topics, with particular interest in men s employment and labor force participation, online gambling/gaming/pornography, modern fatherhood, and social connection, belonging and civic engagement among young men . According to AIBM s published fellowship information, eligible applicants are Ph.D. students enrolled at accredited U.S. universities, with applications welcomed from multiple disciplines and both qualitative and quantitative research traditions. Application Deadline: 15 December 2026. Prospective applicants should review the official AIBM fellowship information carefully for the complete application requirements and submission process. title: 2026 Greening STEM Grant | $5,000 Grants for Schools in the United States
summary: Schools and community partners in selected LyondellBasell communities in the United States can apply for the 2026–2027 Greening STEM Grant , an environmental education funding opportunity designed to support student-centered STEM projects focused on local environmental issues. The initiative is offered through the Environmental Education Initiative (EEI) by Discovery Education , in partnership with the National Environmental Education Foundation (NEEF) and LyondellBasell (LYB) . During the 2026–2027 school year, the initiative will select two cohorts of five Greening STEM projects , with each selected project receiving a $5,000 grant . The programme is designed to engage students in environmental science, encourage informed decision-making about healthy environments, and promote civic engagement through authentic STEM learning experiences. About the Greening STEM Grant The $5,000 grants will support holistic STEM programmes that incorporate environmental science and related resources into school curricula. Projects should focus on student-directed investigations involving relevant research questions, local environmental issues, or challenges affecting local public lands. Funding can help educators develop STEM programming that gives students opportunities to participate in place-based learning and environmental monitoring . The initiative seeks to provide students with authentic STEM learning experiences in which the environment serves as a context for engagement and learning. What the Grant Supports The Greening STEM Grant supports projects that use STEM-focused content, instructional strategies, training approaches, collaboration and dissemination technologies to strengthen learning both inside and outside the classroom. The programme particularly encourages projects that: Introduce middle school students to citizen science or environmental monitoring activities. Build the capacity of formal and informal educators to provide high-quality STEM programming aligned with state education standards. Help schools develop a culture that uses the environment to improve student learning and achievement. Engage young people in environmental monitoring and the collection of environmental data. Give students opportunities to work with data relating to issues such as air, soil or water quality. Develop Science and Engineering Practices, Disciplinary Core Ideas and Crosscutting Concepts. Build partnerships between schools and community-based organizations. Encourage authentic problem-solving, collaboration and student leadership. Increase student interest in STEM subjects and careers. Grant Amount Each selected project will receive: $5,000 The programme anticipates $25,000 in total funding for the fall 2026 grant cycle , supporting five $5,000 grants. Grantees are expected to complete their Greening STEM projects by spring 2027. Funding may support eligible project expenses including: Staff and personnel costs for partner project teams Direct travel costs for project team members Transportation for students and youth participants Training and educational materials Project-specific supplies and materials Measurement equipment Tablets and software Data-quality measures and evaluations Professional development for educators and partner staff On-site project costs Postage and shipping Laboratory analysis of air, soil or water samples Data analysis Training related to programme planning, citizen science and environmental monitoring The source states that no more than 10% of the project budget should support training . Eligibility The grant competition is open to public schools serving Grades 6–12 and their community partners located in the following targeted communities: Houston, Texas Corpus Christi–Victoria–Matagorda, Texas Lake Charles, Louisiana Edison, New Jersey Morris, Illinois Clinton, Iowa Cincinnati, Ohio Applicants must submit their applications through the NEEF online grants system. Greening STEM Project Design Principles Projects should incorporate the Greening STEM Design Principles , which are based on an interdisciplinary and collaborative approach to STEM education. The model places students and their interests at the centre of learning while using natural environments and real-world challenges to encourage exploration, problem-solving and environmental stewardship. Projects should include four key elements: 1. Place-Based Learning Students should explore a topic, issue or problem through direct experience and collaboration. Community partners and educators can help connect students with relevant opportunities and resources. 2. Three-Dimensional Learning Students explore an anchoring phenomenon, question existing assumptions, apply STEM practices and connect disciplinary knowledge with real-world events. 3. Project-Based Learning Students should engage with challenging project work over an extended period while using appropriate tools, techniques and technology. They should also have opportunities to share their findings with audiences beyond the classroom. 4. Community-Based Learning Students examine environmental issues within their local cultural and community context. Projects should consider local perspectives and how proposed solutions may affect the communities involved. Project Expectations Applicants are expected to describe a citizen science or environmental monitoring project and explain the STEM skills students will develop through participation. The project should include: A series of STEM learning activities. Pre-field activities that prepare students for field experiences. At least one pre-field activity involving a virtual or in-person visit to the participating school by a community partner representative. One or more field visits where students participate in data collection as part of citizen science or environmental monitoring. At least two post-field activities. A post-field activity involving data analysis. A presentation of project findings. title: Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027: Apply for a 9-Month AI Policy Fellowship at Imperial College London
summary: The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 is a professional learning and development opportunity designed for senior civil and public servants who want to strengthen their understanding of artificial intelligence and its growing implications for public-sector policy, strategy, regulation, and service delivery. Delivered through the Imperial Policy Forum at Imperial College London , the Fellowship combines in-person learning, expert-led sessions, peer engagement, and an individual research project supported by academic mentors. The programme is designed to help participants move beyond theoretical discussions of AI and apply their learning to real policy challenges within their departments and areas of responsibility. Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing how governments approach public services, regulation, infrastructure, healthcare, security, data, and strategic decision-making. For public-sector leaders, understanding both the capabilities and limitations of AI is becoming increasingly important. The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship provides an opportunity for senior civil and public servants to explore these issues in a structured environment while developing a research project connected to their own professional priorities. The 2027 Fellowship will run from February to October 2027 , with a total duration of nine months . Fellows will combine online learning and activities with in-person days at Imperial College London. Key Programme Details Programme: Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 Institution: Imperial College London Duration: 9 months Programme dates: February–October 2027 Application deadline: Monday, 2 November 2026 Location: London and online Format: Individual research project combined with in-person days at Imperial College London Time commitment: Approximately 6–8 hours per month In-person commitment: Four in-person days throughout the year Fee: £1,500, with no VAT added What Is the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship? The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is a bespoke learning and development programme aimed at senior civil and public servants seeking to develop their knowledge of artificial intelligence and understand how it can affect public-sector work. Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom-based learning, the programme combines structured learning with practical application. There are two main components. 1. In-Person Learning at Imperial College London Throughout the Fellowship, participants attend a series of in-person days at Imperial College London. These sessions are designed to help Fellows: Understand fundamental AI concepts. Examine how AI technologies work and what they are capable of. Consider the implications of AI for public policy. Explore AI-related strategy and regulation. Examine challenges associated with public-sector delivery. Engage with academics and specialists. Discuss ideas and experiences with other Fellows. Reflect on how AI knowledge can be applied to their professional responsibilities. The sessions include expert-led lectures, workshops, discussions and opportunities for interaction with peers and specialists. This structure means that participants are not simply learning about AI in the abstract. They are encouraged to think about how emerging technologies relate to actual policy questions and institutional challenges. 2. Individual Research Project The second major component is an individual research project or guiding question focused on a specific AI policy challenge. The project is Fellow-led , meaning that it is shaped around the participant s own policy priorities and professional objectives. Fellows receive support from one or more academic mentors who provide expert guidance throughout the programme. This allows participants to investigate an issue that is directly relevant to their area of work while benefiting from Imperial s academic expertise and institutional environment. The research component is therefore an important bridge between learning and practical policy development. What Can the Research Project Focus On? The Fellowship provides flexibility in the type of project participants can develop. Potential project formats include: Written recommendations for adopting AI within a particular part of a government department. Co-designing strategic plans or technical solutions for policy challenges. Piloting innovative or experimental AI applications within the public sector. Improving systems and infrastructure for AI, including data storage and management. Organising a facilitated workshop for colleagues within a department or team. Producing a published white paper. This flexibility allows Fellows to connect the Fellowship to real issues they are already encountering in their professional roles. Examples of Previous Research Projects The programme provides examples demonstrating how AI policy research can be connected to practical public-sector challenges. Previous examples include: AI and Food Regulation One project involved piloting an AI model for the Food Standards Agency designed to help organisations identify relevant regulations and the bodies responsible for those regulations. AI, Healthcare and Accountability Another project involved a paper co-written between the MHRA and NHS examining the accountability gap surrounding clinical negligence, product liability and practitioner literacy within the UK healthcare system. Human-Centred AI A collaborative workshop explored human-centred AI design involving the Home Office and Imperial s Collective Innovation Lab . AI and Defence Another example focused on Sovereign AI in Defence , involving Imperial academics, the Trusted AI Alliance and consultation with the UK Ministry of Defence. These examples illustrate the breadth of potential applications for AI policy research across government and public services. Benefits of the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship The Fellowship offers several forms of professional and academic development. Tailored Learning The programme provides a personalised learning experience based on Fellows individual needs and professional interests. This allows participants to focus their learning on issues that are relevant to their roles rather than following a completely generic AI curriculum. Practical Research Experience Fellows undertake a research project supported by an academic mentor. This provides an opportunity to apply AI knowledge to a real policy question and develop practical outputs that can potentially be useful within their departments. Access to Imperial Expertise Participants have the opportunity to learn from faculty and specialists associated with Imperial College London, including experts working across AI-related areas in engineering, medicine and science. Professional Networking The Fellowship brings together civil servants and public-sector professionals who share an interest in AI and related policy challenges. Participants can exchange experiences, develop professional relationships and learn from colleagues working on different policy issues. Public-Sector Focus The programme is specifically designed around the challenges of applying AI within the public sector. This means Fellows can explore questions involving policy, governance, regulation, strategy, implementation and public-sector systems rather than concentrating solely on the technical development of AI. Engagement with the Wider Imperial Community Fellows will also have opportunities to engage with the Imperial Policy Forum and the wider Imperial community. The programme combines these connections with formal learning and individual research, creating an environment in which participants can develop their understanding of AI while applying that knowledge to current policy questions. The Fellowship s activities have also included engagement with Imperial s AI and technology ecosystem. The programme information highlights Fellows visiting Imperial s biomedical engineering facilities and participating in workshops involving AI startups at the Deep Tech White City campus. Who Should Consider Applying? The programme is intended for senior civil and public servants who want to deepen their understanding of AI and its implications for public-sector work. It is particularly relevant to professionals who: Work on policy development or implementation. Have responsibilities involving technology or digital transformation. Work with AI-related regulation or governance. Are responsible for strategic planning. Work in public-sector innovation. Need to understand the implications of AI for their department. Want to investigate a specific AI-related policy challenge. Are interested in developing an evidence-based project connected to AI and public policy. The supplied programme information does not provide a specific nationality, race, or continent-based eligibility restriction. Therefore, those details should not be assumed from the available information. Time Commitment The Fellowship runs for nine months and requires approximately 6–8 hours per month . Participants must also commit to four in-person days throughout the year . The programme therefore combines ongoing engagement with concentrated periods of face-to-face learning at Imperial College London. Where Is the Fellowship Held? The Fellowship uses a hybrid format. Participants engage through: Online activities. In-person sessions. Individual research. Engagement with Imperial s academic and policy communities. The programme location is listed as London and online , with in-person days taking place at Imperial College London. Fellowship Cost The fee for participation in the 2027 Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is: £1,500 The programme information states that no VAT is added to this fee. Application Deadline Applications for the 2027 Fellowship are currently open. The application deadline is: Monday, 2 November 2026 Applicants are instructed to complete the application form and send it to the Imperial Policy Forum at the.forum@imperial.ac.uk . Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials are completed and submitted before the stated deadline. How to Apply Prospective applicants should: Review the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship programme information. Consider how AI relates to their current public-sector responsibilities. Identify a policy challenge or research question that could form the basis of their Fellowship project. Consider what they hope to gain from the programme. Complete the official application form. Submit the completed application to the Imperial Policy Forum before the deadline. The official programme page provides access to both the programme brochure and the 2027 application form . Learn more and apply HERE Why the Research Project Matters A distinctive feature of this Fellowship is that participants are not simply passive recipients of training. The research project gives each Fellow an opportunity to connect their learning to a real-world policy challenge. For example, a participant could investigate how their department might adopt AI responsibly, explore policy requirements for a new technology, examine AI-related data infrastructure, develop recommendations for senior decision-makers, or design a workshop to improve colleagues understanding of AI. The project can therefore become a practical mechanism for transferring learning from the Fellowship into the Fellow s professional environment. A Fellowship Focused on Practical AI Policy The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy and government leadership . As governments and public institutions consider how AI should be adopted, regulated and governed, public-sector professionals increasingly need the ability to understand both the opportunities and challenges associated with the technology. The Fellowship s structure responds to this need by combining: AI fundamentals. Policy analysis. Expert learning. Academic mentorship. Practical research. Peer exchange. Professional networking. Public-sector application. This combination allows Fellows to explore AI from both technical and policy perspectives while maintaining a strong connection to their professional responsibilities. Conclusion The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 provides a structured opportunity for senior civil and public servants to deepen their understanding of artificial intelligence and examine how it can be applied to contemporary public-sector challenges. Running for nine months from February to October 2027, the programme combines in-person learning at Imperial College London, online engagement, expert-led sessions, peer networking and a Fellow-led research project supported by academic mentors. Participants can use the research component to explore practical questions involving AI adoption, policy development, regulation, public-sector systems, strategy and governance. With applications closing on 2 November 2026 , prospective applicants should review the programme requirements, identify a relevant policy challenge and prepare their application well before the deadline. title: Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 – Up to £150,000 for UK-Based Researchers
summary: The Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 provide an exciting opportunity for early- and mid-career researchers based in the United Kingdom to expand their professional networks, strengthen their research and policy engagement skills, and develop innovative responses to some of the world s most complex challenges. Offered by the British Academy in partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace , the fellowship is designed for researchers working across the humanities and social sciences who want to build stronger connections between academia, policymaking, and professional practice. The programme provides successful fellows with the opportunity to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace for a period of 12 months , with placements based in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut , depending on the thematic area and proposed fellowship. With awards of up to £150,000 for 12 months , the Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to support researchers in developing new ideas, building international networks, translating academic knowledge into practical applications, and contributing fresh perspectives to policy challenges. The fellowship is particularly relevant to researchers interested in international affairs, global governance, climate and sustainability, geopolitics, Asian regional affairs, the Middle East and North Africa, international institutions, and other interconnected global challenges. Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 Overview The Global Innovation Fellowships are part of the British Academy s efforts to support researchers in the humanities and social sciences in developing relationships beyond traditional academic environments. The programme seeks to create opportunities where researchers can work directly with organisations operating in policy and practice. Through this approach, fellows can gain exposure to different perspectives and working environments while also contributing their academic expertise to real-world challenges. Key details of the 2026 fellowship include: Fellowship: Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Host organisation: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Funding organisation: British Academy Career stage: Early-career and mid-career researchers Application status: Open for applications Opening date: 22 September 2026 Application deadline: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT Interview date: 8 February 2027 Expected commencement: By September 2027 Possible earlier commencement: March or April 2027 Duration: 12 months Maximum award: Up to £150,000 Number of fellowships: Up to two Potential host locations: Washington, DC; Singapore; or Beirut Applicant location requirement: United Kingdom Academic disciplines: Humanities and social sciences Contact: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk About the Global Innovation Fellowships The British Academy has received funding from the UK Department of Business, Innovation, Science and Trade to support its Innovation Fellowships programme. The Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to help researchers develop their skills, professional networks, and careers outside conventional academic environments. The programme places particular emphasis on creating connections between researchers and organisations in the creative and cultural, public, private, and policy sectors . The fellowship recognises that many of today s major challenges cannot be addressed effectively through a single discipline or institution. Issues such as climate change, sustainability, international security, geopolitical competition, global governance, technology, and regional political and economic transformation often require multiple perspectives. The programme therefore encourages researchers to bring their academic knowledge into a different professional setting while learning from practitioners, policymakers, and other experts. Partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace The fourth call of the Global Innovation Fellowships provides opportunities for selected award holders to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace . Carnegie is an international foreign policy institution whose experts work across different disciplines and regions on major global issues. Its work covers areas including democracy, technology, climate change, international affairs, and regional geopolitical developments. The fellowship is therefore structured to expose successful researchers to an environment where academic knowledge, policy analysis, international engagement, and practical problem-solving intersect. Depending on the subject of the fellowship, researchers may be hosted in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut, with opportunities to engage with Carnegie colleagues and regional programmes. Main Objectives of the Fellowship The Global Innovation Fellowships are designed around a mutually beneficial relationship between the award holder and Carnegie. For fellows, the programme can provide an opportunity to: Develop new professional networks beyond academia. Strengthen connections with policymakers and practitioners. Translate academic research and expertise into practical applications. Develop innovative approaches to policy challenges. Gain experience working within an international policy organisation. Explore new perspectives on complex global issues. Strengthen professional skills relevant to policy and practice. Build relationships with experts working in different regions and disciplines. Increase the practical reach and impact of their research. Develop new collaborations that may continue beyond the fellowship. Improve their ability to communicate academic knowledge to non-academic audiences. For Carnegie, the fellowship provides an opportunity to benefit from the expertise, perspectives, research approaches, and experiences of researchers from the UK humanities and social sciences community. Research Areas for the 2026 Fellowship Applicants are invited to submit proposals in one of four broad thematic areas. 1. Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics The first thematic area focuses on the interconnected challenges associated with climate change, sustainability, and nature . A fellowship in this area would be based in Washington, DC and would examine the relationship between environmental challenges and broader geopolitical developments. Applicants could explore issues surrounding the changing global environment, sustainability challenges, climate-related risks, geopolitical consequences, and innovative approaches to addressing interconnected environmental and international problems. The theme recognises that climate and sustainability challenges are not isolated environmental issues. They can intersect with economics, international relations, security, development, governance, resources, and global cooperation. 2. Global Order and Institutions The second thematic area focuses on questions surrounding global order, disorder, and international institutions . This fellowship would also be based in Washington, DC . Applicants working in this area could investigate different dimensions of the international system, including the functioning and evolution of international institutions, changing global relationships, international cooperation, and the challenges facing existing structures of global governance. The programme notes that there is no single solution to the challenges associated with global order and disorder. Applicants are therefore expected to bring thoughtful perspectives and potentially innovative approaches to understanding these developments. 3. South and East Asia The third thematic area focuses on South Asia, East Asia, and Southeast Asia . A fellowship in this area could be based in either Washington, DC, or Singapore , depending on the proposed work and engagement with Carnegie counterparts. Applicants should have strong expertise in one or more of these regions, including expertise relating to India or China and their regional or global roles. The programme is particularly interested in researchers who can contribute informed perspectives on the political, economic, social, strategic, and international dimensions of developments in these regions. Researchers may also engage with questions concerning the broader role of South and East Asian countries in international affairs. 4. Middle East and North Africa The fourth thematic area focuses on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) . Fellows in this area would work with Carnegie s Middle East Program and could be based in Washington, DC, or Beirut . The fellowship may involve examining major challenges facing the region, long-term geopolitical trends, and possible innovative policy approaches. Applicants should have relevant expertise in the Middle East and North Africa, including the Gulf and Iran . The programme welcomes applicants with particular country or thematic expertise relating to political, social, or economic change. Academic and Professional Background The Global Innovation Fellowships do not prescribe one particular academic discipline. Applicants may come from a broad range of disciplinary, conceptual, and methodological backgrounds. The programme is open to perspectives that may be analytical, policy-oriented, practical, or combinations of these approaches. However, applicants must demonstrate a strong understanding of the issues relevant to their proposed fellowship, including the applicable policy environment and the systemic challenges associated with the subject. This means that applicants should be able to demonstrate more than academic interest in their chosen area. They should be able to explain the wider policy context and show how their expertise can contribute to understanding or addressing the challenges involved. Relevant language skills can be beneficial where appropriate to the proposed research or regional focus, although language skills are desirable rather than mandatory . Who Can Apply for the Global Innovation Fellowships? The programme is specifically designed for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers . To be eligible, applicants must meet several important conditions. UK Residency Applicants must be ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom . This requirement means that the fellowship is not a general worldwide opportunity open to researchers residing in any country. Current Long-Term Appointment Applicants must have a current long-term appointment that will continue for at least the duration of the fellowship award. The applicant must also be based at an eligible UK institution, such as: A Higher Education Institution (HEI); or An Independent Research Organisation (IRO). The institution must be listed as an approving organisation within the British Academy s Flexi-Grant system. If an applicant is successful, the institution will be issued the relevant terms and conditions associated with the award. Career Stage The fellowship is intended for: Early-career researchers; and Mid-career researchers. Applicants should therefore demonstrate an established connection to research as well as a clear rationale for how the fellowship will contribute to their professional development and future career. Humanities and Social Sciences Applicants should be researchers working within disciplines in the humanities and social sciences that are eligible under the British Academy s grant management system. There is no single required disciplinary background. The programme allows applicants to approach the thematic areas from different academic, methodological, conceptual, analytical, policy, and practical perspectives. Who Is Not Eligible? Postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for British Academy grant support under this programme. Applicants must confirm that they are not: Currently working towards a PhD; Awaiting the outcome of a viva voce examination; or Awaiting acceptance of corrections required by examiners. This is an important requirement for applicants who have recently completed or are close to completing doctoral studies. Applicants should carefully assess their status against these requirements before beginning an application. Collaboration Between Academia and Policy One of the central features of the Global Innovation Fellowships is the emphasis on moving knowledge between academic and non-academic environments. The fellowship is not simply intended to provide researchers with another academic research placement. Instead, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie can create value for both sides. Applicants should consider: How their academic expertise can contribute to Carnegie s work. What they can learn from working within a policy-focused organisation. How collaboration can generate new ideas. How their research can be translated into policy-relevant knowledge. How interaction with practitioners can influence their future work. How they can develop new professional networks. How their experience can contribute to their long-term career development. The programme particularly seeks applicants who are willing to explore perspectives outside their established academic environment. What the Fellowship Looks for in Applicants Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate an openness to new ideas and a willingness to experiment with innovative approaches. Important qualities include: Intellectual openness. Willingness to explore new perspectives. Interest in interdisciplinary engagement. Ability to work across academic and non-academic environments. Commitment to challenge-driven work. Interest in policy and practice. Ability to engage constructively with different perspectives. Understanding of the needs and priorities of the partner organisation. A clear interest in knowledge mobilisation and translation. A strong connection between the proposed fellowship and future professional development. Applicants should therefore carefully explain not only what they want to research or explore, but also why working with Carnegie is particularly valuable to their proposed project and professional trajectory. Fellowship Locations The location of the fellowship will depend largely on the thematic area and the nature of the proposed work. Possible locations include: Washington, DC Washington, DC is the proposed location for fellowships focusing on: Sustainability, climate and geopolitics. Global order and institutions. Some work related to South and East Asia. Some work related to the Middle East and North Africa. Singapore Singapore may host fellows working on South and East Asian issues. This provides an opportunity for researchers to engage with regional perspectives and Carnegie counterparts working on Asia. Beirut Beirut may host fellows working on Middle East and North Africa issues through Carnegie s Middle East Program. The location is therefore closely connected to the applicant s thematic expertise and proposed area of engagement. Fellowship Value and Financial Support The British Academy is offering up to two fellowships , each lasting up to 12 months . Each award can be worth up to £150,000 . The awards are offered with Full Economic Costing at 80 percent . The financial support is intended to facilitate a substantial period of engagement with Carnegie and enable successful researchers to undertake the fellowship in an international policy environment. Applicants should carefully consult the official scheme guidance to understand the eligible costs, institutional arrangements, funding conditions, and other financial requirements associated with the award. Fellowship Duration and Start Date The Global Innovation Fellowships are expected to commence by September 2027 . However, an earlier start in March or April 2027 may be possible. Applicants seeking an earlier start date will need to explain how they intend to manage the relocation process within the shorter preparation period. The standard fellowship duration is 12 months . Application Deadline The application deadline for the Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 is: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. It is advisable to review the scheme guidance, eligibility requirements, institutional requirements, and application materials well in advance of the deadline. Interview Date Applicants should also take note of the planned interview date. Interviews are scheduled for 8 February 2027. Applicants should ensure that they are available during this period if invited to an interview. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants interested in the Global Innovation Fellowships should carefully consider how their expertise, proposed area of work, and career objectives align with the programme. A strong application should clearly establish the connection between the applicant s background and the fellowship theme. Applicants should consider addressing the following areas: 1. Clearly Identify the Relevant Thematic Area Determine whether the proposed fellowship fits within: Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics; Global Order and Institutions; South and East Asia; or Middle East and North Africa. The proposal should demonstrate a clear connection to the selected theme. 2. Demonstrate Relevant Expertise Applicants should explain their expertise and experience in the relevant area. This may include academic research, publications, policy engagement, professional experience, regional knowledge, methodological expertise, or practical work. 3. Explain the Policy Context The programme expects applicants to have a solid understanding of the relevant policy landscape. Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the wider systems, institutions, actors, challenges, and policy debates connected to their proposed area. 4. Explain Why Carnegie Applicants should clearly explain why the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is an appropriate partner for their proposed fellowship. The application should demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie could create opportunities for: Knowledge exchange. Collaboration. Professional development. Policy engagement. New research perspectives. Network development. Innovative approaches to complex challenges. 5. Demonstrate Value Beyond Academia Applicants should explain how their proposed fellowship could strengthen interaction between academic research and non-academic environments.
