title: Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme 2027: £1,000 Fully Funded Opportunity for Young People Under 30
summary: The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme 2027 is now preparing to welcome a new group of young people to one of the UK s leading agricultural conferences, offering participants an opportunity to develop professional skills, build valuable networks and engage directly with leaders and emerging voices across agriculture, food, business, science, technology and related sectors. The 2027 programme is particularly significant because it marks 25 years since the OFC Scholars Programme began . For its 2027 edition, the programme is being delivered in partnership with Severn Trent Water and M S , introducing a hybrid programme combining in-person gatherings, online learning and participation in the live Oxford Farming Conference in January 2027. Importantly, the programme is not restricted to people who have studied agriculture or currently work within the farming sector. OFC says it welcomes individuals from non-traditional sectors and backgrounds , as well as people with diverse geographical and academic experiences. Applicants who have never studied an agri-food subject are also encouraged to be considered. The programme is designed to help develop the future generations of agricultural and related-sector leaders , while giving Scholars access to peer networking, skills development, professional exposure and the opportunity to participate in discussions surrounding the future of agriculture. What Is the Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme? The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme is an initiative designed to support and develop young people who have the potential to contribute to the future of agriculture and related industries. Rather than simply providing conference attendance, the programme combines the main OFC conference experience with a wider programme of learning and networking activities. The 2027 programme will use a hybrid model , meaning Scholars will participate through a mixture of: In-person professional and educational events. Online bespoke sessions. Peer-to-peer networking. Skills development activities. The live Oxford Farming Conference. Exposure to people and organisations involved in agriculture and associated sectors. The programme is intended to provide participants with an opportunity to exchange ideas and perspectives while developing practical skills that can support their future careers and leadership ambitions. Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme 2027 Highlights The 2027 programme offers a number of significant benefits to successful Scholars. Key features include: Participation in the Oxford Farming Conference 2027 . Full conference access. Two nights of accommodation. Meals associated with the conference programme. Attendance at the Chair s Welcome Reception . Participation in the Oxford Union Debate . Attendance at the Christ Church dinner . Two dedicated in-person development and networking events. Bespoke online webinars. Peer-to-peer networking opportunities. Skills development training. Exposure to agricultural and food-sector leaders. Opportunities to meet people from different professional, geographical and academic backgrounds. The opportunity to become part of the OFC Scholars community. The programme is limited to a defined number of participants, making the application and selection process competitive. How Many Scholars Will Be Selected? For the standard Scholars Programme, 22 individuals will be selected. These places are funded by individual sponsors, who must nominate a proposed Scholar through the application process. In addition to the 22 standard Scholar places, the 2027 programme will include 8 Breaking Barriers places . The Breaking Barriers places are being funded by OFC, Severn Trent Water and M S and have a separate application arrangement. This means the 2027 programme is designed to provide opportunities for a broader range of young people, including individuals who may not traditionally have had access to major agricultural conferences or professional networks. Previous Oxford Farming Conference Attendance Applicants must also not have previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference . The Scholars Programme is intended to introduce new participants to the conference and provide them with an opportunity to experience OFC for the first time. Therefore, someone who has previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference would not meet the stated requirement for the standard Scholars Programme. Do You Need an Agriculture Degree to Apply? No specific agricultural academic qualification is stated as a requirement. This is one of the programme s key features. OFC explicitly encourages applications from people who have not studied agri-food subjects and says the programme welcomes individuals from outside the agriculture sector. This means that people with backgrounds in areas such as business, technology, science, policy, environmental studies, communications, economics, engineering and other disciplines may potentially be relevant to the programme, provided they meet the stated requirements and are put forward through the appropriate application route. Conference participation and associated Scholar activities. Travel costs are not included Sponsors should be aware that travel expenses are not included in the £1,000 fee . title: Denmark Scholarships for International Students: Erasmus Mundus, Danish Government Scholarships, Fulbright and Other Funding Opportunities
summary: Denmark offers a range of scholarship and funding opportunities for international students who want to pursue higher education, participate in student exchanges, or undertake research at Danish institutions. Funding opportunities are available through national and European programmes, institutional partnerships, exchange programmes, joint degree programmes and other international education schemes. For international students considering studying in Denmark, the available funding routes include Erasmus+, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, Nordplus, Fulbright Denmark, Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students, and the Danish State Educational Support (SU) , subject to the eligibility requirements of each programme. This guide explains the major scholarship and funding options, who can apply, what each programme supports, and where prospective applicants can obtain further information. Denmark Scholarships for International Students International students may be able to receive financial support to study in Denmark through several different programmes. However, there is no single application deadline covering all Denmark scholarships described below. Deadlines, selection procedures and eligibility requirements vary according to the programme, university and study programme. Some scholarships are designed specifically for exchange students, while others support students undertaking full-degree Master s programmes, research, or joint degrees involving Danish and other European institutions. The major opportunities include: Nordplus Erasmus+ Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Fulbright Denmark Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students Danish State Educational Support (SU) Other European scholarship and research databases 1. Nordplus Scholarships and Study Opportunities Nordplus provides opportunities for students enrolled at higher education institutions in the Nordic and Baltic regions to study in another Nordic or Baltic country as part of their degree. The programme is therefore particularly relevant to students whose home institutions are located within the Nordic or Baltic region and whose academic programmes allow for international mobility. Students interested in using Nordplus to study in Denmark should first contact their home university or national educational agency to determine whether their institution participates in the relevant Nordplus arrangements. What does Nordplus offer? Depending on the applicable mobility arrangement, Nordplus can provide an opportunity to: Study in another Nordic or Baltic country. Complete part of an existing degree programme abroad. Gain international academic experience. Experience another higher education system. Participate in regional academic mobility. Students should not assume that simply being enrolled at a Nordic or Baltic institution automatically guarantees funding. The relevant institutional and programme requirements must be checked before applying. For additional information, prospective applicants can visit Nordplus . 2. Erasmus+ Study Abroad Opportunities The Erasmus+ programme provides opportunities for students from the EU/EEA and Switzerland to study abroad as part of their higher education in their home countries. According to the information provided by Study in Denmark, exchange periods can range from 2 to 12 months . This makes Erasmus+ particularly relevant for students who want to gain international study experience without necessarily completing their entire degree in Denmark. Who is Erasmus+ intended for? The programme described on the Study in Denmark scholarship page is primarily aimed at students from: EU countries European Economic Area (EEA) countries Switzerland Students normally participate through their existing higher education institutions rather than applying independently to Denmark as an entirely separate degree student. How does the Erasmus+ process work? Students interested in Erasmus+ should: Contact their home university. Determine whether their institution participates in the relevant Erasmus+ mobility arrangements. Discuss available destinations and study options. Confirm eligibility requirements. Follow the application procedure established by their home institution. Confirm the applicable mobility period and funding arrangements. The European Commission provides additional information about studying abroad through Erasmus+. Applicants can consult the European Commission Erasmus+ study-abroad information . 3. Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree Scholarships The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme is one of the most internationally accessible funding routes connected with Master s-level study in Europe. Unlike some mobility programmes that primarily target European students, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are open to both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA students . This makes the programme particularly relevant to international students from countries in Africa, Asia, the Americas, Oceania and other regions outside Europe, provided they meet the admission and scholarship requirements of the specific Master s programme. What is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master? An Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is an international Master s programme delivered jointly by institutions in different countries. In the Denmark-related opportunities described by Study in Denmark, the Master s courses may be offered jointly by a Danish institution and another European university or higher education institution . Students therefore have the opportunity to participate in an international academic programme rather than studying exclusively within one institution or country. What can the scholarship provide? Depending on the individual Erasmus Mundus programme, scholarships may provide substantial financial support associated with participation in the Master s programme. However, scholarship conditions are not identical across all Erasmus Mundus programmes. Prospective applicants should therefore examine the individual Master s programme carefully to determine: Admission requirements Academic qualifications Scholarship availability Application deadline Required documents Selection criteria Mobility requirements Participating universities Study locations Financial support available How to apply for an Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Applicants do not generally apply through one universal Denmark scholarship application. Instead, students should identify an approved Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme that matches their academic background and then contact or apply directly through the individual programme s official application process. The Study in Denmark information specifically advises students and scholars to contact the individual Erasmus Mundus Master s courses for details concerning scholarships and application procedures. A list of approved Erasmus Mundus Master s courses in Denmark is available through the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue . 4. Fulbright Denmark Grants The Fulbright Denmark programme supports educational exchange between the United States and Denmark and focuses on strengthening cultural and academic understanding through international exchange. The programme is particularly relevant to American scholars and postgraduate students at Master s or PhD level who want to undertake study and/or research in Denmark. What does Fulbright Denmark support? Eligible applicants can apply for a Fulbright grant for an entire academic year of study and/or research in Denmark . The programme can therefore be relevant to postgraduate students and scholars whose academic or research objectives align with opportunities available at Danish institutions. Who can apply? The information provided by Study in Denmark identifies: American scholars American postgraduate students Master s-level students PhD-level students as potential applicants. Applicants should consult Fulbright Denmark directly for the current eligibility requirements, selection criteria and application procedures. Further information is available from Fulbright Denmark . 5. Danish Government Scholarships for Highly Qualified Non-EU/EEA Students One of the most important funding routes for international students is the Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students . Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to support highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. This means that the opportunity can be particularly relevant to international students from countries such as those in Africa, Asia, the Americas and other regions outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland , provided they satisfy the applicable requirements. Importantly, these scholarships are not necessarily awarded to every eligible student. Danish universities administer the scholarships and select the recipients. Eligibility for the Danish Government Scholarship According to Study in Denmark, applicants must meet the following conditions: Be a citizen of a country outside the European Union . Be from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) . Not be a citizen of Switzerland. Be enrolled in a full-degree higher education programme . Have been granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark because of education . The scholarship is therefore different from an ordinary exchange arrangement because it concerns students pursuing a full degree programme in Denmark. Who is not eligible? Study in Denmark identifies several circumstances in which a student is not eligible for a Danish Government Scholarship. You may not qualify if you: Are seeking admission to an Artistic Higher Education Institution . Have a legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens. Hold a residence permit at the time of admission under the specific provisions described in the Danish Aliens Consolidations Act concerning certain family members of foreign citizens. Are eligible for a grant under the Danish State Education Fund. Because residence and immigration rules can be complex, applicants should carefully review the applicable requirements with their chosen Danish institution. Learn More HERE 6. What Does the Danish Government Scholarship Cover? The Danish Government Scholarship has two main components . It may consist of: A full or partial tuition fee waiver , and/or A grant toward living costs . Importantly, not every recipient necessarily receives the same combination or level of support. The exact scholarship arrangement depends on the Danish university administering the award. This is an important point for prospective applicants: being eligible for consideration does not necessarily mean receiving a full scholarship covering every expense. Students should therefore carefully review the scholarship information published by their chosen university. Learn More HERE 7. How the Danish Government Scholarship Application Process Works The scholarships are administered by Danish universities , which are responsible for selecting the students who receive the awards. Consequently, prospective applicants should not treat the scholarship as a single centralized national application. Instead, the recommended approach is to: Step 1: Identify a suitable Danish degree programme Applicants should first identify a full-degree programme that matches their academic background and career objectives. Step 2: Check the university s admission requirements Every university and programme may have its own academic and application requirements. These may include: Academic qualifications Previous degree requirements English-language requirements Programme-specific prerequisites Supporting documents Application forms Application deadlines Step 3: Check scholarship eligibility Applicants should determine whether their nationality and personal circumstances meet the Danish Government Scholarship requirements. Step 4: Review the university s scholarship procedure Because universities administer the scholarships themselves, prospective students should consult the admission and scholarship information provided by their selected institution. Step 5: Submit the required application Applicants should follow the university s instructions carefully and ensure that all required documents are submitted before the applicable deadline. The official Study in Denmark information on higher education institutions can be accessed through Study in Denmark s higher education institutions directory . 8. Is There a Deadline for the Denmark Scholarships? There is no single deadline for all of the scholarship opportunities described on the Study in Denmark page. This is because the opportunities are administered by different programmes, universities and organizations. For example: Erasmus+ deadlines can depend on the student s home institution. Erasmus Mundus deadlines are established by individual Master s programmes. Fulbright Denmark has its own application cycle. Danish Government Scholarship deadlines depend on the relevant Danish university and degree programme. Nordplus arrangements depend on the participating institutions and mobility procedures. Therefore, applicants should not rely on a single national deadline . Instead, prospective students should identify their preferred programme and institution and check its current official application deadline. For students considering the Danish Government Scholarship, this is particularly important because Danish universities determine their own application and scholarship procedures. Learn More HERE 9. Danish State Educational Support (SU) The Danish State Educational Support , commonly known as SU , is another source of educational financial support. However, international students should understand that SU is generally awarded to Danish residents . International students may nevertheless be able to apply for equal status for purposes of state educational support under certain circumstances. Equal status may be granted under: Danish rules European Union law This means that international students should not automatically assume that they qualify for SU simply because they have been admitted to a Danish university. Eligibility depends on the applicable rules and the student s individual circumstances. More information is available through the Danish Education Support Agency . 10. Other Sources of Scholarship Information for Studying in Denmark Students looking for funding to study in Denmark should also explore broader European scholarship databases. The Study in Denmark information points prospective students toward Ploteus , which lists scholarship programmes and educational opportunities for both EU and non-EU students. PhD students and researchers are also encouraged to explore the European Researchers Mobility Portal , now associated with the EURAXESS network. These resources can help prospective students and researchers identify additional opportunities beyond the scholarships administered directly by Danish institutions. Learn More HERE 11. Who Can Apply for These Denmark Scholarship Opportunities? Eligibility differs significantly depending on the programme. There is therefore no single nationality or academic qualification requirement covering all the opportunities. International students from outside Europe Non-EU/EEA students may be eligible for certain opportunities, particularly: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students The Danish Government Scholarship specifically targets highly qualified full-degree students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, subject to the stated conditions. EU/EEA students and Swiss students Students from EU/EEA countries and Switzerland can participate in certain European mobility programmes, including Erasmus+ opportunities described by Study in Denmark. They may also be eligible for Erasmus Mundus programmes, which are open to both European and non-European students. Students from Nordic and Baltic countries Students enrolled at Nordic or Baltic higher education institutions may have opportunities through Nordplus to study in another Nordic or Baltic country. American postgraduate students and scholars Fulbright Denmark is specifically relevant to American scholars and postgraduate students at Master s and PhD level seeking study and/or research opportunities in Denmark. 12. Academic Levels Covered The programmes described cover different stages of higher education. Undergraduate and exchange students Students participating in higher education mobility programmes may benefit from: Erasmus+ Nordplus The exact level and eligibility depend on the participating institution and programme. Master s students Master s-level students may find opportunities through: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Danish Government Scholarships Fulbright Denmark for eligible American postgraduate students PhD students and researchers PhD students and researchers may find opportunities through: Fulbright Denmark European research mobility resources Individual Danish university opportunities Relevant Erasmus-related programmes The exact eligibility requirements should always be verified against the specific programme. 13. Important Considerations Before Applying Students considering studying in Denmark should carefully distinguish between admission , scholarship eligibility and scholarship selection . Being academically qualified for a programme does not necessarily guarantee a scholarship. Similarly, being eligible to apply for a scholarship does not necessarily mean that funding will be awarded. Applicants should consider the following: 1. Confirm your nationality eligibility Check whether your country falls within the programme s eligibility requirements. 2. Confirm your academic level Determine whether the opportunity is designed for undergraduate, Master s, PhD, exchange or research applicants. 3. Check whether the programme is full-degree or exchange-based Some opportunities support students completing part of a degree abroad, while others support students enrolled in a complete degree programme. 4. Check the specific university For Danish Government Scholarships, the individual university plays a central role in administering and selecting scholarship recipients. 5. Check the exact deadline Do not assume that all Danish scholarships have the same deadline. 6. Review funding carefully Determine whether the scholarship provides: Full tuition coverage Partial tuition coverage Living-cost support Exchange funding Research funding Other forms of financial assistance 7. Prepare documents early Depending on the programme, applicants may need academic transcripts, certificates, proof of language proficiency, motivation statements, research information, references and other supporting documentation. 14. Why Denmark Is an Attractive Destination for International Students Denmark has a broad higher education system offering hundreds of programmes taught in English. Study in Denmark indicates that Danish higher education institutions offer more than 500 English-taught study programmes . This provides international students with opportunities to search for programmes that align with their academic interests without necessarily requiring Danish-language proficiency for the programme itself. Students interested in studying in Denmark can explore available programmes through Study in Denmark s programme portal . 15. Useful Official Resources Prospective applicants should use official sources when researching scholarships because eligibility requirements, application procedures and deadlines can change. Erasmus+ European Commission – Erasmus+ Study Abroad Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters European Commission – Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Erasmus Mundus Catalogue EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue Nordplus Nordplus Official Website Fulbright Denmark Fulbright Denmark Danish State Educational Support Danish Education Support Agency Study in Denmark Study in Denmark Deadline There is no single overall deadline for these Denmark scholarship opportunities. Application deadlines vary according to the specific scholarship, university, degree programme or exchange scheme. Applicants should therefore check the official deadline for the particular opportunity they intend to pursue. For Erasmus Mundus, the deadline is determined by the individual Master s programme. For Danish Government Scholarships, applicants should check the deadline published by their chosen Danish higher education institution. Conclusion Denmark provides several pathways for international students seeking financial support for higher education, student exchange, postgraduate study and research. The opportunities range from Nordplus and Erasmus+ mobility programmes to Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, Fulbright Denmark and Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students . One of the most important points for prospective applicants is that these programmes do not operate under one common application system. Each programme has its own eligibility requirements, application procedure, funding structure and deadline. Danish Government Scholarships, in particular, are administered by individual Danish universities, meaning that students must consult the institution and degree programme they are interested in for precise scholarship information. International students should therefore begin by identifying an appropriate study programme, checking whether they meet its academic and nationality requirements, reviewing the available funding options, and then following the official application procedure. For students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, the Danish Government Scholarship and Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters can provide important potential routes to funded Master s-level study, while exchange students and eligible European students may find opportunities through Erasmus+ and Nordplus. American postgraduate students and scholars can also explore Fulbright Denmark for study and research opportunities. Because deadlines and requirements can change, applicants should always verify the latest information directly with the relevant Danish university, programme administrator or official scholarship provider before submitting an application.
